doc: The knowledge file in JSON, with CRLF endings, one line per property, view and row: reading, then one step for every kind of edit, each with its exact splices, then undo back to the input. A list written on one line is created with its first item as its opening, the item and its closing, at one offset, and removed with its last item the same way (FBL 6.2).

steps.doc: Opening and saving without an edit writes the bytes that were read.
A new property goes after the last property, its keys in the binding's order; unset keys are left out.
Renaming a property replaces its name in place.
A property's name cannot be emptied: the binding refuses it and nothing is written.
Changing the type of a property no row has a value for replaces the type alone; no cell needs converting.
Moving a property keeps its bytes: its entry goes, and comes back before the property at the new index.
A new option goes after the property's last option.
Renaming an option replaces its name; the cells and conditions naming it store its id and do not change.
Recolouring an option replaces its colour.
Moving an option to the top of its property's list keeps its bytes.
Removing an option removes, bottom-up, every cell whose value names it by id ('by': 'id'); the option's own entry goes last.
A cell's text is replaced in place.
Clearing a cell's text removes the key; the cell stays, naming its property.
Setting a value on a cell without one inserts the key after the property.
A number is written in its shortest form.
A checkbox is a boolean.
Clearing a checkbox removes the key.
A date keeps the precision it is given and stays a string.
Clearing a date removes the key.
A date and time is replaced with its zone.
Clearing a date and time removes the key.
A time of day is a quoted string in YAML, so that no reader takes it for a number.
Clearing a time removes the key.
A selection stores the option's id.
Clearing a selection removes the key.
Adding one of several values appends an item to the cell's list.
Removing one of several values removes its item; the others stay.
A related row is stored by its id in the property's target file.
Removing the first of several related rows removes its item and the separator after it.
Removing an option removes the items naming it; a list left empty goes with its last item, its container listed first so that the undo puts them back in order.
Changing a property's type writes the new type; the cells are converted by the next change of the same gesture.
A number converted to text: the text key is inserted where the binding's key order puts it and the number key goes; a numeric text is quoted in YAML.
Removing a property removes the cells naming it.
A new row goes after the last row.
The first cell of a row creates its list of cells.
Moving a row keeps its bytes.
A new view goes after the last view.
Renaming a view replaces its name.
Duplicating a view is one new entry holding the copy's settings: its columns, sorts, filter and grouping come with it.
Moving a view keeps its bytes.
Removing a view removes its entry with everything in it.
The active view is the table's own setting.
Hiding a column writes 'visible: false' after its property, in the binding's key order.
A column's width is a number.
Wrapping a column's text writes 'wrap: true' after its width.
A new column goes after the view's last column.
Moving a column keeps its bytes.
Removing the first of two columns removes its entry and the separator after it.
The first column of a view creates its list of columns right after the view's name.
Removing a view's last column removes the list with it.
A new sort goes after the view's last sort; an ascending direction is the default and is not written.
Changing a sort's direction writes the direction after its property.
Moving a sort keeps its bytes.
A new condition goes after the filter's last entry.
Matching any condition rather than all writes 'filterMatch' after the view's name.
A filter group is an entry of the filter with its own 'match'.
The first condition of a group creates the group's list of conditions.
Removing a group removes its conditions with it.
Hiding empty groups writes the setting after 'groupBy'.
The first group put in order creates 'groupOrder' right after 'groupBy'.
The next group in order goes after the last.
Dragging a group to the top moves its entry in 'groupOrder'.
Hiding a group creates 'hiddenGroups' right after 'groupBy'.
Collapsing a group creates 'collapsed' right after 'groupBy'.
Expanding the last collapsed group removes 'collapsed' with it.
Removing a property removes, bottom-up, the cells, conditions, sorts and columns naming it, and a list it leaves empty; the property's own entry goes last.
Removing a row removes its entry with its cells.
